items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: And when Sam died I'd taken his place quite a while with Izil Muggenbaum.

ctx.x: And I played, after I started playing the trumpet, I played a lot of times with him. And when Sam died I'd taken his place quite a while with Izil Muggenbaum. I still moved up from second to first and I played the second.
I see. With the band. Who was Chris's regular drummer then?

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1958-12-22
items.q: Well no, but you see, now Sam Morgan, he used to use that slap stick because he was a funny man about that time.

ctx.x: Is that sort of part of the trumpet's job sometimes to play that?

Well no, but you see, now Sam Morgan, he used to use that slap stick because he was a funny man about that time. He don't, when he set that tempo, he want the drummer to stay right there and then he'd take that, it'd be the same thing like with a guy, the record and the band, but he'd be with that stick and he got to stay with that stick. That slap stick. Yeah. Well I used to use it, but when we was in San Francisco, at the Hangover I don't know. Well you did all the time, I never used it.
You ever used that? Yeah. I used it. I never saw you do it.
